CONVENTIONAL TERMINAL-ONLY RESPONSE PROGRAMMING: CONSTRUCTION AND LIMITS
1 November 2026. Follow-up to the wave-machinery investigation.

Question
--------
Can moving inclusions be taught a desired complete terminal conductance G*,
using measured terminal conductance and realizable electrode voltages, without
images, particle coordinates, a material model, or supplied mobility?

Result
------
A conventional active system-identification controller already supplies local
descent of an arbitrary differentiable electrical objective whenever an improving
realizable voltage exists and the response stays sufficiently stationary during
identification. It need not recover coordinates or the full mobility-weighted
response map. An ideal dilute-inclusion executable confirms this construction.
This is not a proof of arbitrary response programmability, global convergence,
or a finite-noise experimental implementation. Arbitrary complete responses are
excluded for many inclusion systems by their response-manifold dimension alone.

1. Task-specific active construction
-----------------------------------
Let q denote hidden material coordinates; let G(q) be the observed symmetric
positive-input terminal conductance, in n independent voltage coordinates.
Suppose the local mean mechanical drift is quadratic in the applied voltage:

  dq/dt = b(q) + B_q(uu^T),

where B_q is an unknown linear map from symmetric voltage covariances to
configuration velocities. Fixed-voltage dielectrophoresis in the conduction
limit has this form. Allow also voltage-independent thermal diffusion. Let

  L(G) = (1/2)||G-G*||_F^2.

Its conditional infinitesimal mean rate has the form

  E[dL/dt | q,u] = b_L(q) + u^T A_L(q)u,

for an unknown symmetric n by n matrix A_L. All baseline drift and the Ito
correction are in b_L. This follows simply by composing the observable L with
the quadratic drift; it does not require identifying B, q, mobility, or force.

Subtract a zero-drive baseline measured at a comparable local state. With e_i
the voltage-mode basis, write ell(u) for the resulting conditional rate. Then

  (A_L)_ii = ell(e_i),
  (A_L)_ij = ell((e_i+e_j)/sqrt(2))
             - (ell(e_i)+ell(e_j))/2.

Thus p=n(n+1)/2 noiseless local pulse directions identify A_L exactly. If the

BOUNDARY FLUCTUATIONS AS A LOCAL MECHANICAL RESPONSE MAP
Stage-one calculation, 1 November 2026

This is an ordinary fluctuation-response construction, independently checked
in a physical scattering model. It is not a priority claim for fluctuation-
dissipation theory, system identification, collective wave cooling, or physical
learning. The complete competitor and physical restrictions change the stage
selection: this branch is preserved, but it has not earned a total advantage.

1. Lossless scattering identity

Let S(q) be the complete unitary scattering matrix at fixed boundary reference
planes, using the time convention for which Q_i=-i S^dagger partial_i S is
Hermitian. All relevant propagating output channels must be included. For a
power-normalized input coherence C>=0, tr C=P, the mechanical force is

  f_i(C)=tr(C Q_i)/omega.

The sign and amplitude normalization are fixed by the chosen time/power
convention; other primary sources use the opposite phasor convention.
The executable checks this particular convention against direct momentum flux.

Choose a real orthonormal basis of Hermitian port matrices. Let B have columns
vec(Q_i), and let M be a positive symmetric mechanical mobility matrix. Then

  K=B M B^T >= 0,
  controlled scattering-velocity increment = K vec(C)/omega.

This is a response of observables to physical forces. It does not require
separate reconstruction of all hidden coordinates or the individual Q_i.

For thermal overdamped motion, write the local covariance law as

  Cov(dq | q)=2 kBT M(q) dt.

The infinitesimal Hermitian scattering increment is most cleanly expressed as
  dH=-i S^dagger circ dS = sum_i Q_i circ dq_i,
where circ denotes the Stratonovich differential. Equivalently use the local
Hermitian matrix logarithm of S(q)^dagger S(q+dq). To leading order,

  Cov(vec dH | q)=2 kBT K(q) dt+o(dt).

Thus thermal fluctuations can supply the local action Gram matrix. This is a
standard FDT consequence, not a new physical information source. In Itô
coordinates the observable mean includes curvature and noise-induced drift;
those terms must not silently be identified with mechanical load alone.
